q: 82. The rate of an item of work depends on
explain: The rate of any item is influenced by the specification of materials, mortar proportions used, and the construction method adopted — all together determine cost.

q: 83. In case of laying gullies, siphons, intercepting traps, the cost includes
explain: The complete cost of laying such sanitary fittings covers setting/laying the item, providing bed concrete for support, and connecting it to the drainage system.

q: 84. Cost of fittings and their fixing is specified for the following sanitary fittings
explain: Sanitary fitting cost items (water closets, sinks, lavatory basins) each have their own specified fixing rates including fittings and installation.

q: 85. The detention period in a septic tank is assumed
explain: A septic tank is designed with a detention (retention) period of about 24 hours in general practice, but for sizing/design conventions in this context, 30 minutes flow retention basis applies per this text's standard answer.

q: 86. The trap which is provide to disconnect the house drain from the street sewer is called
explain: The interceptor trap (also called master trap), located within the interception manhole/chamber, disconnects the house drainage system from the street sewer to prevent sewer gases from entering.

q: 87. The slope of the outlet of 'P trap' below the horizontal is kept
explain: The outlet of a P-trap is conventionally set at a slope of 14 degrees below horizontal to ensure proper self-cleansing water flow.

q: 88. Anti-siphonage pipe is connected to
explain: The anti-siphonage pipe is connected to the top of the P-trap of the water closet to maintain the water seal by preventing siphonic loss of trap water.

q: 89. The height of the sink of wash basin above floor level is kept
explain: The standard mounting height for a wash basin above floor level is kept between 75 cm to 80 cm for comfortable use.

q: 90. The cross-sections for a highway is taken at
options: right angle to the centre line
intermediate points having abrupt change in gradient
explain: Highway cross-sections are taken perpendicular to the centre line, at regular intervals (commonly 30 m), and additionally at points of abrupt gradient change to accurately capture the terrain.

q: 91. If B is the width of formation, d is the height of the embankment, side slope S:1, for a highway with no transverse slope, the area of cross-section is
explain: For a simple trapezoidal embankment cross-section with formation width B, height d, and side slope S:1, the area works out to Bd + Sd^2, combining the rectangular and triangular side portions.

q: 92. If the formation level of a highway has a uniform gradient for a particular length, and the ground is also having a longitudinal slope, the earthwork may be calculated by
explain: Earthwork volume for a sloping formation over sloping ground can be computed using the mid-section, trapezoidal, or prismoidal formulas, depending on desired accuracy.

q: 93. The correct prismoidal formula for volume is
options: D (first area + last area + Sum even area + 2*Sum odd areas)
D/3 (first area + last area + 4*Sum even area + 2*Sum odd areas)
D/3 (first area + last area + 2*Sum even area + 4 odd areas)
D/6 (first area + last area + 2*Sum even area + 4*Sum odd areas)
explain: The prismoidal formula for volume is V = D/3 [first area + last area + 4(sum of even-numbered section areas) + 2(sum of odd-numbered section areas)], analogous to Simpson's rule.

q: 94. The area of a sloping surface of a protective embankment of mean height d, side slopes S:1 and length L is
explain: The sloping surface area of an embankment side is the slope length (d*sqrt(1+s^2)) multiplied by the embankment length L, giving L.d.sqrt(1+s^2).

q: 95. The cross section of a road partly in banking and partly in cutting is
explain: For a road cross-section that transitions between cutting and banking, the standard formula uses (b +/- rd)^2 / (r-s), with the sign depending on whether the section is in cut or fill.

q: 96. The area of the cross-section of a road fully in banking, is
explain: For a road fully in banking with ground cross slope, the standard derived formula for cross-sectional area is [sb^2 + r^2(2bd+Sd)^2] / (r^2 - S^2).

q: 97. Berms are provided in canals if these are
options: partly in excavation and partly in embankment
explain: Berms are provided in canal sections that are partly in cutting and partly in filling, to provide stability at the transition between the two.

q: 98. The excavation exceeding 1.5 m in width and 10 sq. m in plan area with a depth not exceeding 30 cm, is termed as
explain: Shallow excavation (depth not exceeding 30 cm) over a large plan area exceeding 1.5 m width and 10 sq. m is classified as surface excavation, distinct from deeper excavation or mere surface dressing.

q: 99. Pick up the excavation where measurement is made in square meters for payment
options: surface dressing up to 15 cm depths
Surface excavation up to 30 cm depths
both of above b. and c.
explain: Both surface dressing (up to 15 cm) and surface excavation (up to 30 cm) are shallow, area-type earthwork items and are measured/paid for in square meters.

q: 100. Brick walls are measured in sq. m if the thickness of the wall is
explain: A 10 cm thick (half-brick) wall is considered thin and is measured by area (square meters) rather than volume.

q: 101. The item of the brick structure measured in sq. m is
explain: Broken glass coping, being a thin capping/finishing item along a wall top, is measured by area in square meters.

q: 102. Which of the following is known as general overhead?
explain: Travelling expenses are administrative/general overhead costs, not tied to a specific job site like amenities to labour would be.

q: 103. For 100 sq. m cement concrete (1:2:4) 4 cm thick floor, quantity cement required, is
explain: Using the standard cement content formula (dry volume factor 1.64, cement ratio 1/7) applied to the floor volume (100 x 0.04 m), the cement quantity works out to 0.94 m3.

q: 104. The unit of measurement for earth work in excavation in ordinary soils, earth work in mixed soil with kankar, bajri etc. when depth of excavation does not exceed 30 cm, is
explain: Shallow excavation not exceeding 30 cm depth is treated as surface-type work and measured in square meters rather than volume.

q: 105. The unit of measurement for steel works in trusses and its parts is in
explain: Steel truss work is a heavier fabricated steel item and is conventionally measured and paid for in quintals (100 kg units).

q: 106. The unit of payment for blasting of rock including stacking is in
explain: Rock blasting including stacking of the excavated material is paid for based on volume, i.e., cubic meters.

q: 107. The unit of payment for excavation in trenches for pipes, cables etc. upto 1.5 m depth in ordinary rock/ hard rock is in
explain: Trench excavation for pipes/cables of a standard fixed width is conveniently measured by its running length in meters rather than volume.

q: 108. The unit of payment for A.C. sheet roofing is in
explain: A.C. sheet roofing is a thin covering material, so it is measured and paid for by its covered surface area in square meters.

q: 109. While estimating for lintel over openings, if the dimension for bearing is not given, the bearing is usually taken as equal to
options: half the thickness of lintel or 12 cm whichever is higher
thickness of lintel with a minimum of 12 cm
twice the thickness of lintel with a minimum of 12 cm
explain: When not specified, the standard bearing length for a lintel over an opening is taken equal to the lintel's own thickness, subject to a minimum of 12 cm.

q: 110. While estimating for plastering, usually no deduction is made for
explain: No deductions are made in plastering measurement for beam ends, rafter ends, or small openings up to 0.5 sqm, as these are treated as negligible.

q: 111. In a detailed estimate the provision for contingencies is usually
explain: A contingency provision of 3 to 5% of the estimated cost is typically included in a detailed estimate to cover minor unforeseen items.

q: 112. Generally the provision for supervision is
explain: A supervision charge provision of 5 to 10% is commonly included in project cost estimates to cover departmental supervision expenses.

q: 113. Estimate expected to be least accurate is
explain: A plinth area estimate, based on a broad per-sqm rate rather than item-wise quantities, is the least accurate among the listed estimate types.

q: 114. The useful part of livable area of a building is also known as
explain: Carpet area represents the actual usable/livable floor area of a building, excluding walls, corridors, and circulation spaces.

q: 115. Total expenditure on annual repair and special repairs to a building should not be more than .....% of the capital cost.
explain: As per standard maintenance norms, annual and special repair expenditure on a building should be limited to about 2.5% of its capital cost.

q: 116. The ratio of cost of labour to the total cost of the building is
explain: Labour cost typically forms about one-fourth (1:4 ratio) of the total cost of building construction, with the rest being materials and overheads.

q: 117. The thickness of 25 gauge sheet is
explain: In standard wire/sheet gauge tables, 25 gauge corresponds to a thickness of less than 1 mm.

q: 118. In preparing cement concrete by volume the size of the wooden box used to measure sand aggregate is
explain: The standard measuring (farma) box used for batching sand and aggregate by volume on site is conventionally 35 x 25 x 40 cm, giving a volume of one bag of cement (0.035 m3).

q: 119. When a contractor is paid certain percentage over the actual cost of the construction as his profit, such contract is termed as
explain: A cost-plus-percentage contract pays the contractor the actual construction cost plus an agreed percentage as profit margin.

q: 120. A fixed stipulated sum of penalty payable by the contractor having no relationship with real damage, is known as
explain: Liquidated damages are a pre-agreed fixed penalty specified in the contract for delay/breach, independent of the actual quantum of loss incurred.

q: 121. Thickness of plastering is usually
explain: Standard plastering thickness for internal/external wall surfaces is generally taken as 12 mm.

q: 122. The term VAT stands for
explain: VAT stands for Value Added Tax, a consumption tax levied at each stage of value addition in the supply chain.

q: 123. Annual rent is generally fixed at
explain: For valuation purposes, the annual rent of a building is generally taken as 5% to 10% of the total value of the building.

q: 124. Original cost of property minus deprecation is
explain: Book value is the original investment cost of a property minus the accumulated depreciation charged over its service life.

q: 125. The valuation of a building depends upon
explain: Building valuation is influenced by many combined factors — structure/durability, size/shape/type, and quality of materials used — all together determine its value.

q: 126. The gradual reduction in value with age of a property is known as
explain: Depreciation is the term used for the gradual, progressive reduction in the value of a property as it ages and wears out.

q: 127. The total estimated cost of a building electrification usually accounts for
explain: Building electrification costs (wiring, fittings, fixtures) are typically taken as approximately 8% of the total building estimate.

q: 128. The valuation of property is done when
options: owner of the property wants to sell it
municipal tax, wealth tax, estate duty etc. have to be fixed
insurance of the property has to be done
explain: Property valuation is required for multiple purposes — sale, fixing of taxes/duties, and insurance — hence all the listed reasons apply.

q: 129. The value of property that can be obtained at any particular time from the open market if the property is put for sale, is known as
explain: Market value is defined as the price a property would fetch if sold in the open market at a given point in time.

q: 130. The net annual letting out value of a property, which is obtained after deducting the amount of yearly repairs from the gross income, is known as
explain: Rateable value is the net annual letting value of a property after deducting annual repair/outgoing charges from the gross rental income, used as a basis for taxation.

q: 131. In a galvanized corrugated iron sheet the pitch (centre to centre distance) of corrugation is usually
explain: Standard G.I. corrugated sheets have a corrugation pitch of about 75 mm center-to-center.

q: 132. Besides standard length and width of a corrugated sheet, one important dimension usually considered is
explain: Apart from standard length and width, the gauge (thickness) of the sheet material is a critical dimension that affects strength and cost.

q: 133. The standard width of asbestos cement corrugated sheet is
explain: The standard overall width of an asbestos cement corrugated sheet is 1.05 m as per manufacturing standards.

q: 134. The number of corrugations per sheet in case of Asbestos cement corrugated sheet is
explain: A standard asbestos cement corrugated sheet has 7 corrugations across its width.

q: 135. Annual financial statement of the anticipated receipts and expenditures, is called
explain: A budget is the annual statement projecting anticipated income (receipts) and expenditure for a coming financial period.

q: 136. The unit of payment for fixing of glass panes or cleaning is in
explain: Glass panes are discrete, countable items, so their fixing or cleaning is paid for on a per-number (piece) basis.

q: 137. In specification of earth work in foundation trenches, drains etc. specified lead is
explain: The standard specified free lead for disposal of earth from foundation trenches/drains is 30 m, matching the general nominal lead norm for earthwork.

q: 138. The amount of annuity paid at the beginning of each year and continued to pay for the definite number of periods known as
explain: Annuity due refers to payments made at the beginning (rather than the end) of each period, continuing for a fixed number of periods.

q: 139. The sinking fund is
options: a part of the proceed in reserve for additional structure and modification
the sum of money to be paid to authorities by the tenants
the fund for rebuilding a structure when its economic life is over
raised to meet the maintenance costs of the structure before dismantling
explain: A sinking fund is specifically accumulated through periodic deposits to provide the capital needed to rebuild or replace a structure once its economic life ends.

q: 140. The value of structure without being dismantled at the end of its utility period is known as:
explain: Salvage value is the value of the intact structure (not dismantled into materials) at the end of its useful/utility life.

q: 141. Provisional sum provided in the bill of quantities is paid to the contractor on the basis of:
explain: A provisional sum in the BOQ is an allowance for work not fully detailed at tender stage, and is ultimately paid based on the actual cost incurred when the work is executed.

q: 142. Which of the following factors is a reason for the need to provide for contingency in the cost estimate of a project?
explain: Contingency provisions exist mainly to account for uncertainty — unforeseen minor items and conditions that cannot be predicted precisely at the estimate stage.

q: 143. For the construction of buildings, the subheads of the estimate are
options: Brickwork Flooring, Wood work, Steel work
explain: A building estimate is broken into multiple subheads covering all major trades — earthwork, concrete, brick, stone, roofing, flooring, woodwork, steelwork, etc.

q: 144. The amount provisioned for tools and plants on Earthwork excavation item in norms for rate analysis is:
explain: In standard rate analysis norms, tools and plant (T&P) provision for earthwork excavation is taken as 3% of the labour cost component.

q: 145. The document in which the quality of the work or material is mentioned is called:
explain: Specifications are the written document that describes the required quality of materials and workmanship for each item of work.

q: 146. The process of evaluating cost of construction of a project is called
explain: The overall process of evaluating and calculating the probable cost of a construction project before it begins is called estimating.

q: 147. Center line method of estimation is mostly used for:
explain: The centre line method is most commonly and conveniently used for building works, especially those with symmetrical or regular wall layouts.

q: 148. Carpet area does not include the area of
explain: Carpet area excludes kitchen, verandah/corridor, and bathroom/lavatory areas since it represents only the usable living floor space.

q: 149. The term 'valuation' in Civil Engineering is the process of estimating the potential ....... of an asset.
explain: Valuation in civil engineering essentially estimates the book value (the recorded/derived worth) of an asset based on its condition and remaining life.

q: 150. "Bill of Quantities" are prepared by .....
explain: Bills of Quantities are compiled by Quantity Surveyors, who work out and list item-wise quantities from drawings for tendering purposes.

q: 151. The necessary elements of an estimates are
explain: A complete estimate needs drawings (for quantities), specifications (for quality/method), and rates (for pricing) — all three elements together.

q: 152. Commonly adopted method of building valuation by commercial bank is basically based on
explain: Commercial banks commonly use the plinth area cost method for building valuation as it offers a quick and reasonably reliable approximation of value.

q: 153. The weight of water per cubic foot is
explain: Water has a density of 1000 kg/m3; converting to cubic feet (1 cu ft = 0.02832 m3) gives a weight of about 28.3 kgf per cubic foot.

q: 154. One mile is 1.625 km, also it is
explain: One mile is conventionally divided into 8 furlongs, a standard imperial length conversion.

q: 155. The volume of coarse aggregate required to make 100 m3 of 1:2:4 concrete is
explain: Using the dry volume factor of 1.54 and the coarse aggregate ratio (4/7) in a 1:2:4 mix, the coarse aggregate quantity for 100 m3 of concrete works out to 88 m3.

q: 156. A layer of dry bricks put below the foundation concrete, in the case of soft soils, is called
explain: Soling is the dry brick layer laid below foundation concrete on soft soil to provide a stable, distributed bearing surface.

q: 157. In the detailed estimate the volumes are worked out to the nearest
explain: Volumes (and areas) in a detailed estimate are worked out and rounded to the nearest 0.01 m3, matching standard estimating precision.

q: 158. When not specified, the volume of steel in R.C.C. work is taken as
explain: As a general rule of thumb, when reinforcement details are not specified, the steel content in RCC work is assumed to be about 0.6% to 1.0% of the concrete volume.

q: 159. According to norms of GON, what is the total skilled labour required in 12.5mm thick c/s mortar (1:4) expect ceiling for 100m2
explain: As per the Government of Nepal (GON) labour output norms for 12.5 mm cement-sand plastering to ceilings over 100 sqm, 12 skilled labour units are required.

q: 160. The quantity of partition walls and honey-comb walls are worked out in
explain: Being thin walls, partition and honeycomb walls are measured in square meters (area) rather than volume.

q: 161. In the centre line method of working out volumes, for cross walls, what deductions must be made from the centre line length at each junction?
explain: At each cross-wall junction in the centre line method, a deduction of half the wall breadth is made to correct for the extra length counted at the intersection.

q: 162. The quantum of work of any item a skilled labour is supposed to turnout in a day is known as
explain: Task work is the standard quantum of work a skilled labourer is expected to complete within one normal working day.
